messages:
maria: Quick question — we have ephemeral saved queries (session-only) in Compare mode. If a user accidentally navigates away or the tab crashes, do we want a "Restore ephemeral queries" flow in Console? :thinking:

raj: I think yes, but let's decide where to store recovery state. localStorage is easiest, but it's per-device and fragile. backend TTL (e.g., 24h) would let us show "Recent ephemeral queries" across devices.

laura: From a UX POV, showing "Recovered from last session" with a small badge sounds safe. We should avoid polluting permanent saved queries list. Maybe a separate section: Recent session queries (ephemeral).

tom: Backend + TTL makes sense operationally. We can model ephemeral entries as saved_query objects with flags: {id, owner, query, ephemeral: true, expires_at}. That lets routing/quotas use existing savedquery APIs and keeps snapshot/rollback logic consistent.

raj: Agree. One concern: quotas and telemetry. If we persist ephemeral queries in DB we need to track who created them and enforce per-tenant limits. Otherwise someone could spam ephemeral queries to evade quota.

maria: Good call. We should treat ephemeral saves against the same saved-query quota pool. Also add telemetry events for restore so we can measure how often users rely on it. Suggested events: saved_query.ephemeral.create, saved_query.ephemeral.restore, saved_query.ephemeral.expire.

tom: Sketch of API we discussed:
```
POST /api/v1/saved_queries
{
  "query": "route:payments model:gpt-4o prompt:...",
  "ephemeral": true,
  "ephemeral_ttl_seconds": 86400
}
```
GET /api/v1/saved_queries?scope=ephemeral&owner=current_user
```
This uses existing auth and listing endpoints — minimal backend changes.

raj: Implementation note: ephemeral objects still need to be included in the indexing/permissions layer so the Console can filter by route/model when showing recents without scanning the whole tenant. Otherwise list performance will suffer.

laura: UX question: when a user restores an ephemeral query, do we convert it to a permanent saved query automatically or only after they click "Save"? I'd prefer not to auto-convert; explicitly show "Save this query" CTA so users remain in control.

maria: Agreed. Restore = populate workspace + banner "Recovered from last session — Save? [Save] [Dismiss]". We should also provide a small undo.

raj: Edge case: if user had multiple ephemeral queries across routes, how to surface them? We can group recents by route/model and show a compact list under "Recovered queries" in the saved queries panel.

tom: Ops implications: expiration job needs to be idempotent and emit telemetry on cleanup. Also we should shard TTL removal to avoid big delete bursts during maintenance windows.

maria: Rollout plan idea: behind feature flag first. Expose to 5% of Console users, log telemetry, watch restore success and churn. If recovery rate > 5% and low/no abuse, widen rollout.

raj: Add quota tests: ensure ephemeral saves count toward per-tenant saved_query_count and rate limits. Also add unit tests for the API to reject malformed ephemeral_ttl (min=60s, max=7 days).

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: feature/ephemeral-savedqueries flagged on staging at 2024-06-12T18:00Z.

laura: I'll mock UI (compact recovered list + restore banner) and drop designs in Figma by EOD Thursday.

maria: Action items: tom to prototype DB shape + TTL job, raj to update quota checks & telemetry, laura to produce mocks. We'll sync next Tue for API contract sign-off. Thanks :+1:
